agent_notes: This uncommitted diff is close to a full revert of HEAD 542d5dd, whose message says the separate-form layout caused 'saving never submitted them'. It deletes the explanatory comments that described the constraint. Nothing in the diff or commit history authorizes going back.

The page already uses the form= attribute for the same reason: the add-instance controls (lines 226-250) associate with forms outside the main settings form because nested <form> is illegal HTML (comment at line 248). The deleted settings-form link followed that pattern; the replacement does not.

The Security form (save_security, lines 97-114) still separates the General block from the instances block. So the two save_settings halves cannot be merged into one literal <form> without moving the Security section. If a single literal form is the goal, the Security section would have to move above General or below the instances; that would be a layout change and a product decision.

Suggested debt follow-up, not a finding: save_settings handles partial payloads asymmetrically (it preserves instances but resets General to defaults). That makes any future split of the template unsafe, so mirroring the instance fallback for General would reduce the risk.
No new dependencies, import changes or cycles. The change is template-only.

agent_notes: Blast radius: one template (settings.html) and one handler (save_settings, routes.py:520). It affects every user of the Settings page, every time they press Save Settings.

Mechanism: save_settings rebuilds config['general'] entirely from the submitted form, with no merge against current_settings except for tracking_delay_seconds (routes.py:537). Missing General keys therefore become defaults rather than 'unchanged'. The template-side association is the only thing keeping General values intact.

Persistence: the reset values pass pydantic validation and are written atomically to config.toml, then applied live (setup_logging, scheduler reconfiguration). This is durable config data loss, not a display glitch.

Behavioral consequences of the reset: skip_unreleased flips to False, so unreleased media gets searched. hard_max_per_cycle drops to 0, which removes the cap. request_timeout and page_size revert to 30 and 50, and log_level reverts to info.
Security form (save_security, line 97) is unaffected. It remains a separate, valid form. Add-instance forms (line 250) are unaffected.
No schema, migration or performance impact.
Verdict: blocking. This diff re-introduces the exact bug fixed in HEAD (542d5dd). Discard it.
